summary: A short note from Alex McKenzie at BBN that attaches network traffic statistics for the ARPANET for August 1972. The tables show how many packets each host sent over the period. It updates RFC 378. BBN had been giving these figures to ARPA each month and now shared them with the whole network community.

plainLanguage.summary: This is a monthly tally from the early internet, showing how many packets each computer sent. Think of counting how many letters each house mailed in a month, so the post office can see where the traffic is.

questions: how much traffic did each arpanet host send
subtitle: A one-page table of ARPANET traffic for August 1972, host by host, sent out by BBN.

tldr.problem: Network participants wanted to see how much traffic each site on the ARPANET handled.
tldr.mechanism: Alex McKenzie attaches a table for August 1972 that gives, per host, internode traffic, intranode traffic, the total and an average daily internode figure over 31 days.
tldr.outcome: The table totals 21157570 internode and 8926549 intranode. The RFC updates RFC 378.

today: RFC 391 updates RFC 378 and records one month of 1972 only. It is a historical measurement, not a specification.

sections.title: The August 1972 Statistics
sections.content:
RFC 391 is a short note from A. McKenzie dated 15 September 1972. Its abstract says it attaches the network traffic statistics for the month of August 1972. It updates RFC 378.

There is no protocol here, only the table.
sections.plainLanguage: A short note with a table showing how busy the network was in August 1972.

sections.title: How the Table Is Laid Out
sections.content:
Each site such as UCLA, SRI, UTAH or BBN has one line per host. The columns are inter-node, intra-node, total, avg. daily internode and days. Sites with several hosts get a subtotal row.

Most sites show 31 days. Some report no traffic at all: TINK, MC CL and BELV are listed as having no traffic.
sections.plainLanguage: Each place gets a row, and the columns say how much was sent between computers, how much stayed inside one, and the totals.

sections.title: Network Totals
sections.content:
At the bottom the table gives overall figures. The total is 21157570 internode and 8926549 intranode. The daily average is 682502 internode and 287953 intranode. The average per node-day is 23535 and 9929.

A last line gives packets per message (internode) as 1.09. The RFC does not explain the units further.
sections.plainLanguage: The bottom row adds everything up, so you can see how much the whole network handled in the month and on an average day.
